resolutions.researcher_notes: Live opec.org PDF is dead (redirects to homepage) -- confirmed known gotcha. Recovered via Wayback + pdftotext (url_verifier's automated substring check false-negatives on both snapshots because it runs requests' raw .text decode against the PDF's binary bytes rather than parsing it -- confirmed by reading url_verifier.py; this is a tooling limitation, not evidence the pages lack the data). Manually extracted with `pdftotext -layout`: OPEC ASB2017 (2016 data) Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016' lists 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2), Mellitha Oil & Gas, Eni Oil, 2 x 82 [mi], 34, 10 [in]' -- i.e. the pipeline is carried in OPEC's live-infrastructure gas-pipeline table as of year-end 2016. OPEC ASB2013 (2012 data) Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012' independently lists the same route ('Bu–Attifel/Intesar, Mellitah Oil and Gas, 82.46, 34, 4,134,806, na') five years earlier. The route appears continuously across OPEC's annual gas-infrastructure tables from 2012 through 2016 data -- status inferred as operating from sustained inclusion in these operational tables (not a literal 'operating' string match, per the status-inference rule). tier=medium and independent=false because both citations trace to the same publisher (OPEC ASB); no independent (non-OPEC) source specifically describing this inland Sirte Basin gathering line's operational status could be located -- WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted) and direct fetches of Libya Herald, NOC.ly, and Wikipedia (Sirte Basin) did not surface pipeline-specific operational reporting.

OPEC ASB2013 (2012 data) Table 4.10 row 'Bu–Attifel/Intesar, Mellitah Oil and Gas, 82.46, 34, 4,134,806, na' gives Capacity = 4,134,806 -- an EXACT digit-for-digit match to the sheet's 4134806.00 (table header labels the capacity column '(1,000 scm/yr)', so the underlying physical capacity is arguably 4.13 billion scm/yr, but the sheet's raw number matches OPEC's raw table entry exactly, which is what the ref needs to support). VALUE CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: OPEC ASB2012 (2011 data, one year earlier) lists the SAME route with a different capacity, 11,328,236 -- nearly 2.7x higher. That earlier row also gives a length of 133 mi (vs 82.46/82 mi in the 2013/2017 editions) that matches the *oil*-pipeline Bu-Attifel/Intesar entry in the same 2012 bulletin's Table 4.9, suggesting the 2012 edition's gas-table row for this route was miskeyed/copied from the oil-pipeline table rather than independently re-surveyed. The 2013 and 2017 editions agree with each other on length (~82 mi) and diameter (34in), and only the 2013 edition states a capacity, which matches the sheet exactly -- treating ASB2012's row as the outlier/error rather than citing it. tier=medium, independent=false: only one usable OPEC edition supports this exact figure and no non-OPEC corroborating source for pipe capacity could be located (WebSearch unavailable this session).

Sheet value LengthKnown=131.96 km. OPEC ASB2017 (2016 data) Table 9.9 gives the Bu Attifel/Intisar 34in gas line as '2 x 82' miles (rounded); 82 mi x 1.60934 = 131.97 km -- essentially an exact match to 131.96 km. OPEC ASB2013 (2012 data) Table 4.10 gives the same route as 82.46 mi; 82.46 mi x 1.60934 = 132.68 km, also close (within ~0.5%). Both editions are internally consistent with each other and with the sheet once the miles-header column is converted to km (the header literally says '(miles)'; this is a genuine miles value here, unlike some other Sirte-Basin rows in these same tables where the 'miles' column appears to actually hold km -- cross-checked against the ASB2012 edition's outlier '133' entry for this same route, which does NOT convert cleanly and looks like a copy-over error from the oil-pipeline table, see Capacity notes). tier=medium/independent=false: both citations are OPEC ASB editions; no independent non-OPEC source giving this line's length could be located this session (WebSearch budget exhausted; Wikipedia has no dedicated article on this pipeline or Abu Attifel field).

Wikipedia's Sirte Basin article lists both 'Bu Attifel Field' and 'Intisar Field' in its Sirte Basin oil/gas field data table (Eastern province fields, discovered 1968/1967 respectively), independently confirming both endpoints sit within the Sirte Basin, Libya. OPEC ASB (2012 data, Table 4.10) separately lists the 'Bu–Attifel/Intesar' gas line under its Libya section alongside the other Sirte-Basin gathering lines (Zueitina, Waha, Sirte Oil-operated routes), confirming the route connects these two named fields within Libya. Two independent origins (Wikipedia field-geology article vs. OPEC transportation statistics) agree the two endpoints are Libyan Sirte-Basin oil/gas fields, though neither source names a more granular administrative unit than 'Sirte Basin' -- consistent with the sheet's StartState/Province='Sirte Basin' (no district-level field given in the brief to independently check further).

OPEC ASB (2012 and 2016 data editions) both list 'Mellitah Oil and Gas' / 'Mellitha Oil & Gas' as owner/operator of the Bu-Attifel/Intisar gas line -- matches sheet Operator exactly (spelling variant 'Mellitha' vs 'Mellitah' is a transliteration variant, same company). Libya's National Oil Corporation's own official subsidiaries page (noc.ly/companies-subsidiaries/) independently lists the company in Arabic as 'شركة مليته للنفط والغاز بي . في' (Mellitah Oil and Gas B.V.), which matches the sheet's OperatorLocalLanguage field closely (minor spacing/diacritic differences typical of transliteration). Two independent origins (OPEC statistics vs. NOC's own corporate site) confirm both the English and Arabic operator names.

Eni's own Libya operations page lists 'Mellitah Oil & Gas BV' as a company operating in Libya with 'National Oil Company (NOC)' as partner -- confirms the two-party NOC/Eni JV structure but does NOT state the 50/50 split explicitly for Mellitah O&G BV. Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article states the sister Eni-NOC venture, the Western Libya Gas Project, 'is a 50-50 joint venture between NOC and Eni' -- the standard, publicly-documented equity split for NOC/Eni upstream-gas joint operating companies in Libya, of which Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V. (operator across Wafa, Bahr Essalam, El Feel, Bouri and the Sirte Basin fields including Abu Attifel) is the umbrella JV entity. Could NOT find a source stating the 50%/50% split for Mellitah O&G B.V. by name specifically (as opposed to the WLGP sub-project) -- WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted at 200/200) and targeted fetches of Eni's site, NOC's site, and Wikipedia (Eni, Bouri Field, Greenstream pipeline) all confirm the NOC-Eni JV relationship without stating Mellitah's own percentage. tier=medium reflecting that the exact 50/50 split is inferred from the well-established NOC-Eni JV pattern rather than confirmed for this legal entity by name; flagging for Baird/maintainer that a source naming Mellitah O&G B.V.'s exact equity split specifically would strengthen this to high.
